items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Don opened in Connie's with all the musicians that had recorded with him except Red Allen, Leonard Davis and myself. His three trumpets were Sidney de Paris, Shirley Clay and Langston Curl.

ctx.x: Don recorded 4 numbers with a band that included Leonard 'Ham' Davis, Red Allen and myself on trumpet, Claude Jones, Fred Robinson and Benny Morton, trombones, Edward Inge, clarinet and alto, Rupert Cole, alto, Bob Carroll, tenor, Horace Henderson, piano, Talcot Reeves, guitar, Manzie Johnson, drums, Bob Ysaguire, bass, Lois Deppe and Don, vocals. The titles were 'Chant of the Weed ', 'Shaking the African ', 'I Heard' and

The only trumpet solos were done by Red Allen and when these records came out with the names of the musicians, Langston Curl's name was on the cover instead of Bill Coleman. It probably happened because I never joined Don's band before.

After the recordings were made I did not hear anything from Don. Bobby Neal was working in a small dancing school and asked me to join him which I did. A couple of weeks later Bobby Ysaguire came to see me and said that Don was rehearsing at Connie's Inn and wanted me to join the band. I didn't think it was correct on my part to leave Neal so soon after I had joined him and explained this to Bobby.
